addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- entire-search: Search Entire checkpoint history and transcripts with `entire search --json`. Use proactively when the user asks about previous work, commits, sessions, prompts, or historical context in this repository. (Tools: Bash)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

- anthropic-skills:consolidate-memory: Reflective pass over your memory files — merge duplicates, fix stale facts, prune the index.
- anthropic-skills:docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx files) or Word templates (.dotx files). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, headings, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, performing find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file, use this skill. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation.
- anthropic-skills:explain-usage: Explain where this session's tokens went, with one simple chart in plain language. Use when the user says things like "explain my usage", "where did my tokens go", or asks for a usage breakdown.
- anthropic-skills:morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.
- anthropic-skills:pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email or summary); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user mentions "deck," "slides," "presentation," or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. If a .pptx or .potx file needs to be opened, created, or touched, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:schedule: Create or update a scheduled task that runs automatically. Use when the user says things like "every day", "each morning", "remind me in an hour", "run this at noon", or wants to reschedule an existing task.
- anthropic-skills:setup-cowork: Guided Cowork setup — install role-matched plugins, connect your tools, try a skill.
- anthropic-skills:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- anthropic-skills:xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation

# Agent Guide — Cakebrew

export const meta = {
  name: 'cakebrew-polish-audit',
  description: 'Audit Cakebrew across polish dimensions and draft verified GitHub issues',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Audit', detail: 'parallel auditors, one per polish dimension' },
    { title: 'Verify', detail: 'adversarially check each finding against the real code' },
    { title: 'Synthesize', detail: 'dedup, rank, and draft issue bodies' },
  ],
}

const REPO = '/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/cakebrew'

const CONTEXT = `
You are auditing Cakebrew, a native macOS GUI for Homebrew, at ${REPO}.
It is Objective-C / AppKit. Read AGENTS.md FIRST — it encodes maintainer decisions you must respect.

Key facts (do NOT propose work that contradicts these):
- Minimum deployment target is macOS 15; builds against the latest SDK. Do not propose lowering/pinning.
- The app is deliberately NOT App-Sandboxed (measured decision, documented in AGENTS.md). Never propose sandboxing.
- Sparkle and PXSourceList were deliberately removed. Do not propose re-adding Sparkle.
- Distribution is Developer ID + hardened runtime + notarized via .github/workflows/release.yml.
- A privileged XPC helper (CakebrewHelper) exists with code-signing pinning and SMAppService registration.
- Testing: unit tests in CakebrewTests/, XCUITest journeys in CakebrewUITests/ against a -BPMockBrew mock interface.
- Recent completed work (do NOT re-file): casks support (browse/install/uninstall/upgrade/all-casks), pinned formulae + pin badges,
  services view (brew services), Preferences window, background updater with dock badge + notifications, doctor view,
  shell-injection fix, tap-name validation, privacy manifest, sheets-not-modals conversion, unified/transparent Tahoe toolbar.

The goal: what remains to make this a genuinely polished, delightful, best-in-class Mac app.

RULES:
- READ-ONLY. Do not edit, write, or create any file. Do not run git commands that mutate state.
- Every finding must cite concrete evidence: file path + line number, or a named absent capability you verified is absent by searching.
- Prefer specific, actionable, independently-shippable units of work over vague aspirations.
- Do NOT propose anything that already exists. Search before claiming absence.
- Skip trivia (whitespace, comment nits). Aim for things a discerning Mac user or reviewer would actually notice.
`

const FINDINGS_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    findings: {
      type: 'array',
      items: {
        type: 'object',
        properties: {
          title: { type: 'string', description: 'Imperative issue title, under 70 chars' },
          area: { type: 'string' },
          problem: { type: 'string', description: '2-4 sentences: what is wrong or missing today, concretely' },
          proposal: { type: 'string', description: 'What to build/change. Specific enough to start work from.' },
          evidence: { type: 'string', description: 'file:line citations, or the exact searches proving absence' },
          user_impact: { type: 'string', enum: ['high', 'medium', 'low'] },
          effort: { type: 'string', enum: ['small', 'medium', 'large'] },
        },
        required: ['title', 'area', 'problem', 'proposal', 'evidence', 'user_impact', 'effort'],
      },
    },
  },
  required: ['findings'],
}

const VERDICT_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    verified: {
      type: 'array',
      items: {
        type: 'object',
        properties: {
          title: { type: 'string' },
          area: { type: 'string' },
          problem: { type: 'string' },
          proposal: { type: 'string' },
          evidence: { type: 'string' },
          user_impact: { type: 'string', enum: ['high', 'medium', 'low'] },
          effort: { type: 'string', enum: ['small', 'medium', 'large'] },
          verdict: { type: 'string', enum: ['CONFIRMED', 'REJECTED'] },
          verdict_reason: { type: 'string' },
        },
        required: ['title', 'area', 'problem', 'proposal', 'evidence', 'user_impact', 'effort', 'verdict', 'verdict_reason'],
      },
    },
  },
  required: ['verified'],
}

const DIMENSIONS = [
  {
    key: 'hig',
    prompt: `Audit macOS HIG conformance and visual/interaction polish.
Look at: the xibs (Cakebrew/**/*.xib, MainMenu.xib), BPToolbar, BPStyle, BPMainWindowController, BPSideBarController,
BPHomebrewViewController, BPSelectedFormulaViewController, the Views/ directory.
Consider: window state restoration, sidebar/inspector idioms for macOS 15/26, toolbar customization, search field behavior,
empty states, loading/progress affordances, contextual menus, drag & drop, Quick Look, sheets vs popovers, dark mode,
the app icon (check Assets.xcassets — is it still a generated placeholder from Tools/generate-placeholder-appicon.swift?),
Dock menu, Services menu, Share menu, Touch/menu bar extras, About panel, first-run onboarding, Help book.
Also audit the main menu: missing standard items, missing keyboard shortcuts for frequent actions.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'a11y',
    prompt: `Audit accessibility and internationalization.
Accessibility: search for accessibility APIs (accessibilityLabel, setAccessibilityLabel, accessibilityIdentifier,
NSAccessibility protocols) across Cakebrew/ and the xibs. Assess VoiceOver labeling of toolbar items, sidebar rows,
table columns, badges, the pin glyph, progress/output text views. Check full-keyboard-access navigation,
focus rings, Increase Contrast / Reduce Motion / Reduce Transparency handling, and whether any color alone conveys meaning.
Internationalization: check all six Cakebrew/*.lproj/Localizable.strings for missing/untranslated keys and for
English strings hardcoded in .m files that never route through NSLocalizedString. Check date/number/plural formatting.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'features',
    prompt: `Audit feature completeness versus what Homebrew can actually do and what users of a brew GUI want.
Read BPHomebrewInterface.h/.m, BPHomebrewManager, BPListMode, the BPHomebrewInterfaceListCall subclasses, and the sidebar enum.
Enumerate brew capabilities NOT surfaced: e.g. brew bundle (Brewfile dump/install), brew deps/uses dependency graphs,
brew leaves, autoremove, brew search of the remote catalog, tap management UI, formula options/args on install,
cask zap vs uninstall, brew analytics toggle, brew cleanup scoping, pinning casks, version pinning/switching (brew switch),
outdated-with-greedy handling, formula caveats display, install-time progress detail, brew doctor remediation,
per-formula install/upgrade history, brew --prefix/multiple prefix support, Apple Silicon vs Intel prefix handling.
For each gap, verify it is genuinely absent (grep the codebase) before filing. Prioritize by how much a real user would want it.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'correctness',
    prompt: `Hunt for real correctness and robustness bugs.
Focus: BPHomebrewInterface.m (async command execution, output blocks, nil handling), BPTask.m (process lifecycle,
termination, pipe draining, deadlock on large output), BPHomebrewManager.m (cache invalidation, reentrancy, the
24h disk cache allFormulae.cache.bin), BPBackgroundUpdater.m (timer lifecycle, notification auth), the Helper/ XPC
code (BPHelperSecurity, connection invalidation, privilege boundary, argument validation), BPFormula parsing.
Look for: main-thread violations on UI updates, retain cycles in blocks, use-after-free, unbounded memory on large
brew output, race conditions between reload and user action, unhandled brew exit codes / partial failures,
error paths that silently swallow failures, state that desyncs when brew is upgraded or the prefix moves,
missing cancellation for long-running operations. Each finding needs a concrete failure scenario.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'perf',
    prompt: `Audit performance and perceived responsiveness.
AGENTS.md notes 'brew casks' can take 80+ seconds cold, with a 24h disk cache. Read BPHomebrewManager.m's
reloadFromInterfaceRebuildingCache:, the cache read/write path, BPFormulaeDataSource (filtering/search over large arrays),
BPFormulaeTableView, and BPTask output streaming.
Assess: cold-launch time to usable UI, whether the whole UI blocks during a reload, incremental vs all-or-nothing loading,
search/filter cost on 8000+ formulae, table view cell reuse and attributed-string cost, memory footprint of the full catalog,
whether the disk cache is atomic/corruption-safe and versioned, redundant brew invocations, and whether progress is
communicated during long operations. Propose concrete, measurable improvements.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'architecture',
    prompt: `Audit code health and architecture, with an eye to sustainable future work.
Survey the whole Cakebrew/ tree. Look for: dead code and unused declarations, god objects (check the line counts of
BPHomebrewViewController.m, BPHomebrewInterface.m, BPMainWindowController.m), duplicated logic across the
cask/formula code paths, stringly-typed brew argument construction, missing nullability annotations and lightweight
generics, ObjC patterns that predate modern idioms, the app/helper transport switch and whether the two paths can diverge,
error propagation (NSError vs logging), the singleton graph and its testability, and whether Swift interop is set up
for incremental migration. Also check .travis.yml (stale?), Dependencies/, and build settings for warnings that
should be enabled (e.g. -Wall/-Wextra, treat-warnings-as-errors, static analyzer, sanitizers in CI).`,
  },
  {
    key: 'quality-gates',
    prompt: `Audit testing, CI, release engineering, and product surface quality.
Read .github/workflows/ci.yml and release.yml, scripts/, CakebrewTests/ and CakebrewUITests/, README.md.
Assess: unit-test coverage gaps by file (which source files have zero tests), whether BPMockHomebrewInterface covers
every interface method, UI-test journey gaps for shipped features (services, preferences, casks, pinning, background updater),
crash reporting / diagnostics for users, in-app update mechanism now that Sparkle is gone (how does a user learn a new
version exists? verify what exists today), version/build stamping, the release checklist, README accuracy and screenshots,
CHANGELOG/release notes, issue and PR templates in .github/, CONTRIBUTING, licensing/attribution, Homebrew-version
compatibility testing, and static analysis in CI. Do not propose re-adding Sparkle; propose what fits a notarized
Developer ID app instead.`,
  },
]

phase('Audit')

const audited = await pipeline(
  DIMENSIONS,
  d => agent(`${CONTEXT}\n\n=== YOUR DIMENSION: ${d.key} ===\n${d.prompt}\n\nReturn 5-10 findings, highest value first.`,
    { label: `audit:${d.key}`, phase: 'Audit', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA }),
  (result, d) => {
    if (!result || !result.findings || !result.findings.length) return { key: d.key, verified: [] }
    return agent(
      `${CONTEXT}\n\nYou are an adversarial verifier for the "${d.key}" audit of Cakebrew. Another agent produced the findings below.
Your job is to REFUTE each one by checking the actual code. Reject a finding if:
- the capability it claims is missing actually exists (search hard before trusting the claim);
- the cited file:line does not support the claim;
- it contradicts a documented maintainer decision in AGENTS.md;
- it duplicates work already completed (see the completed-work list above);
- it is too vague to act on, or is pure trivia.
Default to REJECTED when uncertain. For CONFIRMED findings, correct any inaccurate evidence, tighten the title,
and sanity-check the effort/impact ratings.

FINDINGS:
${JSON.stringify(result.findings, null, 2)}`,
      { label: `verify:${d.key}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA }
    ).then(v => ({ key: d.key, verified: (v && v.verified) || [] }))
  }
)

const confirmed = audited
  .filter(Boolean)
  .flatMap(r => (r.verified || []).map(f => ({ ...f, dimension: r.key })))
  .filter(f => f.verdict === 'CONFIRMED')

log(`${confirmed.length} findings survived verification across ${DIMENSIONS.length} dimensions`)

phase('Synthesize')

const synthesis = await agent(
  `${CONTEXT}\n\nYou are the maintainer's editor. Below are verified audit findings for Cakebrew from 7 independent auditors.

Produce a final, deduplicated, ranked backlog of GitHub issues that together would take this app from "solid" to
"polished and genuinely delightful Mac app".

Requirements:
- MERGE near-duplicates across dimensions into one issue each. Findings from different auditors often describe the same work.
- Drop anything that is not worth a maintainer's time.
- Aim for 15-25 final issues. Each must be an independently shippable unit of work (the repo's rule is one PR per logical unit).
- Rank by (user impact / effort), highest first.
- For each issue write:
  * title: imperative, under 70 chars, no issue-number or emoji
  * labels: 2-3 from this set only: enhancement, bug, ui, accessibility, performance, tech-debt, testing, ci, docs, security
  * body: GitHub-flavored markdown with these sections in order:
      ## Problem   (what a user or maintainer hits today, concretely, with file references as \`path:line\`)
      ## Proposal  (what to build; bullet the steps)
      ## Acceptance criteria  (a checklist of - [ ] items, testable)
      ## Notes  (constraints from AGENTS.md that apply: TDD, mock-interface override needed, six .lproj files,
                 sidebar enum renumbering, sheets-not-modals, no sandboxing — include only what actually applies)
  * priority: P0 | P1 | P2
  * effort: small | medium | large
- Also write a short 'roadmap' string: 3-5 sentences framing the backlog as themed milestones.

FINDINGS:
${JSON.stringify(confirmed, null, 2)}`,
  {
    label: 'synthesize-backlog',
    phase: 'Synthesize',
    schema: {
      type: 'object',
      properties: {
        roadmap: { type: 'string' },
        issues: {
          type: 'array',
          items: {
            type: 'object',
            properties: {
              title: { type: 'string' },
              labels: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
              body: { type: 'string' },
              priority: { type: 'string', enum: ['P0', 'P1', 'P2'] },
              effort: { type: 'string', enum: ['small', 'medium', 'large'] },
            },
            required: ['title', 'labels', 'body', 'priority', 'effort'],
          },
        },
      },
      required: ['roadmap', 'issues'],
    },
  }
)

return { roadmap: synthesis.roadmap, issues: synthesis.issues, rawConfirmedCount: confirmed.length }

content.text:
15 agents, 64 verified findings, distilled to **30 issues**. Everything is staged and pinned to `scottdensmore/Cakebrew`.

## The blocker

```bash
gh auth refresh -h github.com -s repo
```

```bash

```

That creates the labels then files all 30 with `--repo scottdensmore/Cakebrew` explicit on every call. Say the word and I'll run it myself once auth is live.

## What the audit found

Five themed milestones. The headline: **there are live P0 defects on the most-used paths**, not just polish gaps.

**M1 — Stop the bleeding (P0)**

| # | Issue | Effort |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fix Upgrade All Outdated, which passes brew an empty argument | small |
| 2 | Stream brew output live: fix BPTask pipe reads and split UTF-8 | medium |
| 3 | Append to the log text views and fix lost Doctor output | small |
| 4 | Stop rebuilding the full catalog after pin, unpin and doctor | small |
| 5 | Update the brew info parser for modern Homebrew output | medium |

I verified 1–4 personally. Worth your attention on two:

- **Upgrade All is broken, and your own security fix broke it.** [BPInstallationWindowController.m:223](Cakebrew/Controllers/BPInstallationWindowController.m:223) still does `upgradeFormulae:@[@""]` with the comment "recycling API with empty string". That worked when arguments were space-joined — the empty string vanished. Since the injection fix, [formatArguments:](Cakebrew/BPHomebrewInterface.m:226) passes them as positional parameters through `brew "$@"`, so it survives. Live shell check prints `[upgrade]` then `[]`, and `brew upgrade ''` errors out. No test caught it because `BPMockHomebrewInterface` overrides `upgradeCasks:` but not the formula path.
- **Nothing streams, and the app can wedge.** [BPTask.m:185](Cakebrew/BPTask.m:185) answers the data-available notification with `readDataToEndOfFile`, which blocks until brew exits — so every log sits blank until it's over. Worse, that same thread is parked in `waitUntilExit`, so while it's stuck on one pipe the other never drains; brew fills 64 KB, blocks on write, and can't exit. There's no Cancel button (issue 15). Your helper transport already does this correctly with `availableData` — the direct path never got the fix.
- **Doctor output is silently discarded.** [BPDoctorViewController.m:57-61](Cakebrew/Controllers/BPDoctorViewController.m:57) captures `previousString` *after* clearing the view, so it's always `@""` and each chunk overwrites the last. You only ever see the final chunk.

**M2 — Feels like a Mac app (7–14)** · Dark Mode hardcoded colors, split divider resetting on every click, missing sidebar toggle + duplicate ⌘F, dead column headers, search that ignores casks, wrong localized strings.

**M3 — Trustworthy operations (15–19)** · Cancel control, brew failures currently reported as silent success, mock coverage for mutating commands (+ gating the mock out of Release), catalog cache serving stale data as fresh.

**M4 — Fast and legible (20–22)** · Ten serial brew invocations per reload → concurrent, incremental publishing with real progress, VoiceOver and Full Keyboard Access.

**M5 — Ship-ready identity (23–30)** · Real app icon (still the generated placeholder from PR #9), version stamped from the release tag, About credits and README, then cask zap, cleanup dry-run preview, Dock menu and Brewfile support.

Every body has Problem / Proposal / Acceptance criteria / Notes, with the AGENTS.md constraints that apply called out per issue — TDD ordering, mock overrides, the six `.lproj` files, sidebar enum renumbering. Bodies are at `scratchpad/issues/01.md`–`30.md` if you want to edit any before filing.

content.text:
All 30 issues are filed and verified on [scottdensmore/Cakebrew](https://github.com/scottdensmore/Cakebrew/issues) — **#67–#96**, labeled by type, priority, and effort (5 × P0, 20 × P1, 5 × P2).

Two things I changed beyond filing, both worth knowing:

- **Enabled Issues on the repo** (per your go-ahead). It was off because GitHub disables issues on forks by default — the tracker is now publicly visible on your fork.
- **Created 16 labels**: the ten type labels, `P0`/`P1`/`P2`, and `effort:small|medium|large`.

## Where I'd start

[#67 Fix Upgrade All Outdated](https://github.com/scottdensmore/Cakebrew/issues/67) — it's small, it's the app's headline action, and it's currently broken in a way that's easy to miss: your shell-injection fix (PR #58) changed argument passing from space-joined to positional `"$@"`, which made the long-standing `upgradeFormulae:@[@""]` hack at [BPInstallationWindowController.m:223](Cakebrew/Controllers/BPInstallationWindowController.m:223) start sending brew a real empty argv entry. Verified live. A regression test at the argv seam prevents it recurring, and it exposes the missing mock override that let it through untested.

Then [#68](https://github.com/scottdensmore/Cakebrew/issues/68) — it's the only P0 that can actually wedge the app, since the single-threaded pipe read in `BPTask` can deadlock on a chatty install with no Cancel to escape.

One pattern across the P0s worth naming: your XPC helper transport already handles streaming correctly (`availableData` + a split-UTF-8 hold-back buffer), while the direct `BPTask` path — the default for shipping builds — never got those fixes. #68 proposes sharing one decoder rather than maintaining two divergent implementations, and #16/#82 covers the mock gaps that let this class of bug through CI.

The raw audit data (64 verified findings, per-dimension) is at `scratchpad/backlog.json` if you want the detail behind any issue.

  --title "Fix Upgrade All Outdated, which passes brew an empty argument" --body "$(cat << 'EOF'
Closes #67.

## What was broken

"Upgrade All Outdated" recycled the named-upgrade API by passing `@[@""]`
(`BPInstallationWindowController.m:222`, comment and all). That was harmless
while arguments were joined into the shell command string — the empty string
simply vanished.

#58 then moved arguments to the shell's positional parameters (`brew "$@"`) to
close the injection hole, and the empty string started surviving as a real argv
entry. Confirmed against real Homebrew:

```
$ /bin/zsh -l -c 'brew "$@"' brew upgrade --dry-run ""
Error: No such file or directory @ rb_check_realpath_internal -
```

So the app's headline "upgrade everything" action has been failing outright.
No test caught it because `BPMockHomebrewInterface` overrides `upgradeCasks:`
but not `upgradeFormulae:` — the mock fell through to the real implementation
and would have shelled out to brew.

## What changed

- `+argumentsForUpgradingFormulae:` / `+argumentsForUpgradingCasks:` build the
  argv and drop blank operands. No operands means bare `brew upgrade`, which is
  how you ask Homebrew to upgrade everything outdated.
- The call site passes `nil` instead of `@[@""]`.
- Added the missing `upgradeFormulae:withReturnBlock:` mock override, streaming
  `MOCK_UPGRADE_OK`, so this path can never shell out under `-BPMockBrew`.
- Bare `brew upgrade` covers outdated casks too, so the confirmation copy now
  says so. Each locale's existing translation was **extended**, not replaced —
  "casks" stays untranslated per AGENTS.md.

## Testing

`BPUpgradeArgumentsTests` (10 cases) was written first and failed to compile on
the new selectors, then covers the regression directly: the empty string,
whitespace-only names, and blanks mixed into a real selection, plus
pass-through ordering and the `--cask` variants.

- Build: **zero warnings**
- Unit suite: **154 tests, 0 failures**
- Verified end-to-end with `brew upgrade --dry-run` — old argv errors, new argv
  runs clean. No real upgrade was run.
- Mock build launched and inspected visually; all six locales verified in the
  built bundle's compiled `.strings`.

The UI journey for Upgrade All is left for #81 (Cancel control), since the
existing upgrade UI test cancels at the confirmation sheet and never reaches
the operation.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -3

content.text:
Here's the chain — `Claude.app` → `Helpers/disclaimer` → `claude` (Claude Code) → `zsh` → `osascript`. That `disclaimer` helper matters: it's Apple's mechanism for a parent to disclaim TCC responsibility, so the permission gets attributed to the **Claude** app itself rather than to `osascript`.

## What to do

Open the pane:

```bash
open "x-apple.systempreferences:com.apple.preference.security?Privacy_Accessibility"
```

Look for **Claude** in the list and switch it on. If it's not listed, click **+**, press ⇧⌘G, and add `/Applications/Claude.app`. Then **quit and reopen Claude** — TCC grants aren't picked up by an already-running process, so this session will restart.

I can't do any of this for you: it's a system security setting, it needs your password, and changing those is off-limits for me by design.

## Two things to weigh first

**The grant is not scoped to Cakebrew.** Accessibility access lets the granted app synthesize clicks and keystrokes into *any* application and read window contents system-wide — your mail, your browser, your password manager. You'd be giving my shell that reach, permanently, until you revoke it. That's a real expansion of what I can do on your Mac, and it's worth deciding deliberately rather than because it unblocks one screenshot.

**There's probably a better payoff than screenshots.** Your AGENTS.md records this quirk:

> Local XCUITest runs often die at init with "Timed out while enabling automation mode" (machine-level permission issue).

That is almost certainly this same missing permission. If so, granting it doesn't just let me poke menus with `osascript` — it makes the **local UI-test suite actually run**, which is the sanctioned harness, already has journeys written, and asserts far more rigorously than me eyeballing a PNG. That would be worth updating AGENTS.md over, since it currently tells every agent that local UI verification is impossible.

So my suggestion: grant it, then let me try `xcodebuild test -scheme CakebrewUITests` first. If that starts working, driving the UI by hand becomes mostly unnecessary — and for a case like #97's German confirmation string, an XCUITest assertion on the sheet is better evidence than a screenshot anyway.

If you'd rather not widen the permission, the status quo is not bad: CI is already the authoritative UI gate per your own workflow, and it caught nothing wrong with #97.

Either way, [PR #97](https://github.com/scottdensmore/Cakebrew/pull/97) is still green and waiting on the `gh` token before I can merge it.

content.content:
## Problem

Nothing streams. `Cakebrew/BPTask.m:185` responds to `NSFileHandleDataAvailableNotification` by calling `-readDataToEndOfFile`, which blocks until the child closes the pipe — so the notification registered at `:107-113` and `:122-128` buys nothing and the whole transcript arrives at once when brew exits. The operation sheet, Update pane and Doctor pane sit blank for the entire run.

Worse, the thread parked in `[self.task waitUntilExit]` (`Cakebrew/BPTask.m:170`) is the same run loop that delivers these notifications, so while it is stuck inside one read the *other* pipe is never drained. stdout and stderr are independent `NSPipe`s (`:92-99`); once brew fills the unread pipe's 64 KB buffer it blocks on write and can never exit — with no cancel affordance, that is a wedged app.

Each chunk is also decoded with `initWithData:encoding:NSUTF8StringEncoding` (`Cakebrew/BPTask.m:206`) with no fallback, so a read boundary splitting a multi-byte sequence silently drops the chunk. brew prints checkmarks and arrows routinely. The helper transport already solves both problems correctly — `availableData` in a readability handler (`Cakebrew/Helper/main.m:94-98`) and a hold-back buffer (`Cakebrew/Helper/BPHelperOutputRelay.m:40-66`). The direct BPTask transport is the default for non-sandboxed shipping builds (`Cakebrew/BPHomebrewInterface.m:275-292`), so this is the live path.

## Proposal

- Switch the handler to `-availableData` and re-arm with `waitForDataInBackgroundAndNotify`, treating a zero-length read as EOF; or move BPTask to `readabilityHandler` blocks on a dedicated queue, matching `Helper/main.m`.
- Drain both pipes independently so neither can back-pressure the child.
- Extract the split-sequence hold-back from `BPHelperOutputRelay` so both transports share one decoder.
- Set `task.standardInput` to `/dev/null` — `inputPipe` at `Cakebrew/BPTask.m:34` is declared and never referenced anywhere in the tree.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test feeding `/bin/sh -c` output on both stdout and stderr (>64 KB each) receives all bytes and the task terminates
- [ ] A test asserts chunks are delivered to the update block *before* process termination
- [ ] A multi-byte character split across a chunk boundary is delivered intact (mirroring `BPHelperOutputRelayTests`)
- [ ] The split-UTF-8 decoder is shared between the direct and helper transports
- [ ] Installing a formula shows output appearing progressively in the operation sheet

## Notes

TDD: the streaming and split-sequence tests are written first. `BPHelperOutputRelayTests.m` is the model for the decoder test. No behavior change to the helper transport, whose signature pinning must stay intact.

git -c commit.gpgsign=false commit -q -F - << 'EOF'
Stream brew output live and stop BPTask deadlocking on a full pipe

BPTask answered NSFileHandleDataAvailableNotification with
-readDataToEndOfFile, which blocks until the child closes the pipe. Three
consequences, all on the shipping (direct) transport:

- Nothing streamed. The operation sheet, Update pane and Doctor pane sat
  blank for the whole run and the transcript appeared at once at the end.
- The reading thread parked in one pipe never drained the other. Once
  brew filled the unread pipe's 64 KB buffer it blocked on write and
  could never exit — a wedged app with no cancel affordance. The
  no-update-block path had the same shape: stdout to end, then stderr.
- Chunks were decoded with -initWithData:encoding: and no fallback, so a
  read splitting a multi-byte sequence (brew prints ✔/✘/→ constantly)
  returned nil and dropped the chunk.

Adopt the pattern the helper transport already proved: a readability
handler per pipe feeding BPHelperOutputRelay, then detach and drain the
tail after waitUntilExit. Both pipes now drain independently, and the
relay's hold-back buffer is the single shared decoder for both
transports — BPHelperOutputRelay.m joins the app target for it.

Chunks are delivered on a private serial queue, and -execute waits for
that queue to drain before returning. This is load-bearing:
-performSyncBrewCommandWithArguments: copies the buffer its block filled
the instant -execute returns, so delivery must be both ordered and
complete by then. The old updateBlockQueue property worked against both
guarantees — it was only ever set to a concurrent queue, which could
reorder chunks and race on the NSMutableString — so it is removed along
with the now-dead queue: parameter.

Also set standardInput to the null device; the child had the app's stdin
attached and nothing ever wrote to it, so anything reading stdin hung.

BPTaskStreamingTests drives a real /bin/sh: a gated script that can only
exit if a chunk arrived mid-run, >64 KB down both pipes at once with and
without an update block, and multi-byte characters split across reads.
On the old code four of the six fail by timeout.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git log --oneline -1
git push --no-verify -u origin fix/bptask-streaming 2>&1 | tail -3

content.content:
## Problem

All three streaming log views replace the text view's entire document on every chunk.

- `Cakebrew/Controllers/BPInstallationWindowController.m:157-170` accumulates the whole transcript in a block variable and calls `setString:` with all of it via `performSelectorOnMainThread:...waitUntilDone:YES`, blocking the producer thread on the main thread. Cost is quadratic in transcript length, all on the main thread, and `BPAutoScrollTextView.m:13-17` re-scrolls on every set.
- `Cakebrew/Controllers/BPUpdateViewController.m:62-66` does the same.
- `Cakebrew/Controllers/BPDoctorViewController.m` is outright broken: `previousString` is captured at `:61` *after* the view is cleared at `:57`, so it is always `@""` and every chunk overwrites the previous one. All but the last chunk of `brew doctor` output is lost.

For VoiceOver users, replacing the document also throws the review cursor back to the top on every update, making a running log unreadable.

## Proposal

- Replace `setString:` with an append into the view's `textStorage` (one `replaceCharactersInRange:withString:` at the end plus `scrollRangeToVisible`).
- Coalesce chunks in a buffer flushed on the main queue at ~30-60 Hz; drop `waitUntilDone:YES` for an async dispatch.
- Fix the Doctor capture so output accumulates.
- Cap scrollback so a long upgrade cannot grow unbounded.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test feeding N synthetic chunks into each controller's output block asserts the full concatenation is present, in order
- [ ] A Doctor-specific test asserts multi-chunk output is not truncated to the last chunk
- [ ] No `setString:` remains on the streaming paths; producer thread is never blocked on the main thread
- [ ] Scroll position follows the tail and the view remains responsive with a 100k-line transcript

## Notes

TDD: the doctor-truncation test is the red case to write first. Pairs naturally with the BPTask streaming fix but is independently shippable — this issue is about what the view does with chunks, not how they arrive.

content.thinking:
Now I see all three sites replace the whole document, so I'm designing an append API for `BPAutoScrollTextView` that lets callers append text from any thread while following the tail, using a coalesced pending buffer protected by a lock so updates get batched and applied on the main queue.

For flushing, I'll append the buffered text to the text storage, scroll to the end, and trim scrollback once it exceeds a cap—settling on roughly 2,000,000 characters, trimming the oldest 25% at once rather than repeatedly deleting small amounts, since a 100k-line transcript could run several megabytes and needs to stay responsive. I also want tests that feed many chunks through each controller's output block and verify the behavior.

Testing view controllers is heavy since it requires loading nibs, so a better seam is to put the coalescing/append/trim logic directly in the NSTextView subclass, which I can instantiate headlessly in a test bundle without a window. Since the flush is scheduled asynchronously on the main queue but XCTest also runs on the main thread, I'll expose a public `flushPendingOutput` method that tests can call directly to apply buffered output immediately, keeping the append method itself simple—just buffering and scheduling a flush.

I also need to fix the Doctor view controller by removing its broken previousString capture and switching it to use appendOutput:, along with doing the same for the Update and Installation paths. Rather than writing a heavy test against BPDoctorViewController and its Homebrew interface dependency, I think the more durable regression guard is a view-level test confirming that appending multiple chunks yields the correct concatenation, since moving to appendOutput: eliminates the original defect class entirely.

Actually, there's a hermetic path: extract the output-handling block into a separate method like appendOutputChunk: that each controller calls, then test that method directly by instantiating the controller and asserting the text view content after repeated calls. The catch is whether nib loading works in the test bundle since the nibs live in the app bundle, so I need to check if the test target has access to those resources.

Given that uncertainty, I'll be pragmatic: move the scroll/append/coalescing/trim logic into BPAutoScrollTextView with thorough unit tests, switch all three controllers to use it and delete Doctor's broken capture, and note in the PR that controller-level tests aren't hermetic so the guard lives at the view seam instead. That covers the substance of the requirements even without full controller-level testing.

Two of the four are done and committed locally. Auth is still dead, so I'll pause here rather than pile up more unpushed work.

## Done and committed locally

**#68 — `32eeab4`** Streaming and the deadlock.
The reading thread answered "data available" with `readDataToEndOfFile`, which blocks until the child closes the pipe — so nothing streamed, and while parked on one pipe the other was never drained. Fixed by adopting the pattern your helper transport already proved: a readability handler per pipe feeding `BPHelperOutputRelay`, then detach and drain the tail after exit. The relay joins the app target, so its split-UTF-8 hold-back is now the one shared decoder for both transports.

The subtle part: `-execute` is synchronous and `performSyncBrewCommandWithArguments:` copies its buffer the instant it returns, so chunk delivery has to be both **ordered and complete** by then. Chunks now go through a private serial queue that `-execute` drains before returning. `updateBlockQueue` worked against both guarantees — it was only ever set to a *concurrent* queue, which could reorder chunks and race on the `NSMutableString` — so it's gone, along with the now-dead `queue:` parameter. Also pointed the child's stdin at the null device.

6 tests driving a real `/bin/sh`; four of them fail by timeout on the old code. Suite went from 86s of timeouts to 0.36s.

**#69 — `ac47e55`** Log views.
`-appendOutput:` on `BPAutoScrollTextView`: any thread, buffered in order, one `textStorage` edit per flush, no `waitUntilDone:`, 2 MB scrollback cap trimmed at a line boundary. Three controllers converted; their outlets retyped from `NSTextView` to the class the xibs have always instantiated.

For the Doctor truncation I made the mock stream **three** chunks instead of one, so `testRunningDoctorShowsOutput` now requires the first *and* last marker in the same view — on the old code the first is gone. That turns an existing UI test into the exact regression guard the issue asked for.

Verified across both: **169 unit tests, 0 failures, zero warnings**, and I ran the *real* app against real brew — 147 installed, 8549 formulae, 7704 casks all populate, which exercises the rewritten sync path well past the 64 KB buffer that used to deadlock.

gh pr create --repo scottdensmore/Cakebrew --base main --head fix/bptask-streaming \
  --title "Stream brew output live and stop BPTask deadlocking on a full pipe" --body "$(cat << 'EOF'
Closes #68.

## What was broken

`BPTask` answered `NSFileHandleDataAvailableNotification` with
`-readDataToEndOfFile`, which blocks until the child closes the pipe. Three
consequences, all on the direct transport that shipping builds use:

- **Nothing streamed.** The operation sheet, Update pane and Doctor pane sat
  blank for the whole run; the transcript appeared all at once at the end.
- **The app could wedge.** The reading thread parked in one pipe never drained
  the other. Once brew filled the unread pipe's 64 KB buffer it blocked on
  write and could never exit — with no cancel affordance (#81). The
  no-update-block path had the same shape: stdout to end, *then* stderr.
- **Chunks could vanish.** Decoding with `-initWithData:encoding:` and no
  fallback returns nil when a read splits a multi-byte sequence, and brew
  prints ✔/✘/→ constantly.

## What changed

Adopted the pattern the helper transport already proved (`Helper/main.m`): a
readability handler per pipe feeding `BPHelperOutputRelay`, then detach and
drain the tail after `waitUntilExit`. Both pipes drain independently, and the
relay's hold-back buffer becomes the single shared decoder for both transports
— `BPHelperOutputRelay.m` joins the app target for it.

**The delivery guarantee is load-bearing.** `-execute` is synchronous and
`-performSyncBrewCommandWithArguments:` copies the buffer its block filled the
instant `-execute` returns, so delivery must be ordered *and* complete by then.
Chunks now go through a private serial queue that `-execute` drains before
returning. `updateBlockQueue` worked against both guarantees — it was only ever
set to a concurrent queue, which could reorder chunks and race on the
`NSMutableString` — so it is removed, along with the now-dead `queue:`
parameter it fed.

Also set `standardInput` to the null device: the child had the app's stdin
attached and nothing ever wrote to it, so anything reading stdin hung.

## Testing

`BPTaskStreamingTests` drives a real `/bin/sh` rather than a stub:

- a gated script that can only exit if a chunk arrived mid-run
- >64 KB down both pipes at once, with and without an update block
- multi-byte characters split across reads
- non-zero exit status, and stdin seeing EOF

Four of the six fail by timeout on the old code (86s of timeouts → 0.36s after).

- Build: **zero warnings**
- Unit suite: **160 tests, 0 failures**
- Ran the **real** app against real brew: 147 installed, 8549 formulae, 7704
  casks all populate — the rewritten sync path, well past the 64 KB buffer.

Progressive rendering in the sheet is not yet observable end-to-end: the views
still replace their whole document per chunk, which #69 fixes.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -2

Closes #69.

> **Stacked on #98.** Base is `fix/bptask-streaming` so the diff shows only this
> change. Once #98 merges I'll retarget this to `main` and rebase.

## What was broken

All three streaming log views replaced the text view's entire document on every
chunk — quadratic in transcript length, on the main thread, and it throws
VoiceOver's review cursor back to the top on every update. Two of them also
blocked the producer thread with `performSelectorOnMainThread:waitUntilDone:YES`.

`BPDoctorViewController` was outright broken: it captured `previousString`
*after* clearing the view, so the captured value was always `@""` and every
chunk overwrote the previous one. All but the last chunk of `brew doctor` was
silently discarded.

## What changed

Appending is now the text view's job. `BPAutoScrollTextView` gains
`-appendOutput:`, callable from any thread, which buffers chunks in arrival
order and applies them to the text storage as **one edit per flush** rather
than one per chunk — no `waitUntilDone:`. Scrollback is capped at 2 MB and
trimmed from the top at a line boundary, so a long upgrade can't grow the
storage without bound.

The three controllers switch to `-appendOutput:` / `-clearOutput`, and their
outlets are retyped from `NSTextView` to `BPAutoScrollTextView` — the class the
xibs have always instantiated.

## Testing

`BPAutoScrollTextViewTests` covers ordering, coalescing into a single edit,
clearing a buffered-but-unflushed chunk, the cap keeping the tail, and
appending from a background thread.

For the Doctor truncation, the mock now streams **three** chunks instead of
one, and `testRunningDoctorShowsOutput` requires the first *and* last marker in
the same text view. On the old code the first marker is gone, so that existing
UI test becomes the regression guard.

- Build: **zero warnings**
- Unit suite: **169 tests, 0 failures**

**Not visually verified.** This is a UI change and AGENTS.md asks for a visual
check, but `osascript` has no assistive access on this machine, so I couldn't
drive the Doctor pane and watch output scroll. The append logic has unit
coverage and the accumulation has the UI test, but CI's UI job is the real gate
here — worth a human glance at a running install before merge.

content.content:
## Problem

Fourteen mutating operations end with `-sendDelegateFormulaeUpdatedCall` (`Cakebrew/BPHomebrewInterface.m:520, 527, 534, 545, 552, 559, 566, 573, 580, 587, 594, 606, 617, 645`). That lands in `-homebrewInterfaceDidUpdateFormulae`, which unconditionally calls `reloadFromInterfaceRebuildingCache:YES` (`Cakebrew/BPHomebrewManager.m:290-293`). The `YES` short-circuits the guard at `Cakebrew/BPHomebrewManager.m:95`, forcing both `brew formulae` and `brew casks` — the catalogs AGENTS.md documents as 80+ s cold.

So pinning a formula (`:587`), unpinning it (`:594`) or running Doctor (`:606`) — none of which can change catalog membership — re-fetches both full catalogs plus all eight list calls and `brew services list --json`. `runBrewImportToolWithPath:` posts the reload *before* running the import (`:642-647`), so it observes pre-import state.

Compounding it, `-homebrewManagerFinishedUpdating:` clears `currentFormula` and reselects the sidebar row on every reload (`Cakebrew/Controllers/BPHomebrewViewController.m:473-496`), so an unnecessary rebuild also discards the user's selection and detail pane — and the loading overlay is long gone (`:211`, `:468-469`), so it happens with no feedback at all.

## Proposal

- Pass `shouldRebuildCache:NO` for pin, unpin, doctor, install, uninstall, upgrade and export; reserve `YES` for `brew update`, tap, untap and bundle import.
- Move the import reload to *after* the command completes.
- Add targeted refreshes: pin/unpin refresh only `kBPListPinned`; install/uninstall refresh installed/outdated/leaves.
- Preserve the table selection when the reload did not change the current list.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A mock-backed test asserts which `BPListMode` calls are issued after each operation type; pin/unpin/doctor issue no catalog fetch
- [ ] Pinning a formula does not re-run `brew formulae` or `brew casks`
- [ ] The selected formula and detail pane survive a post-operation reload
- [ ] Bundle import's reload runs after the import completes

## Notes

TDD via `BPMockHomebrewInterface` — assert the list modes requested. Note that service operations already deliberately skip the reload (`Cakebrew/BPHomebrewInterface.m:470-472`) and `runCleanupWithReturnBlock:` posts nothing; leave both as they are.

Stop rebuilding the full catalogs after pin, unpin, doctor and installs

Fourteen mutating operations ended in -sendDelegateFormulaeUpdatedCall,
which landed in -homebrewInterfaceDidUpdateFormulae and unconditionally
called reloadFromInterfaceRebuildingCache:YES. The YES short-circuits the
cache guard, forcing both `brew formulae` and `brew casks` — the catalogs
AGENTS.md documents as 80+ seconds cold.

So pinning a formula, unpinning it, or running Doctor — none of which can
change which packages exist — refetched both full catalogs plus all eight
list calls, with no progress shown and the user's selection discarded.

The decision now lives in one tested place. Only commands that change
catalog *membership* — update, tap, untap, bundle — ask for the refetch;
install, uninstall, upgrade, pin, unpin, doctor and export do not, and
unknown commands default to the cheap path so a new operation cannot
silently reintroduce the stall. The delegate call carries that flag
through to the manager.

Two related fixes in the same path:

- runBrewImportToolWithPath: posted its reload *before* running the
  import, so the refresh observed pre-import state and nothing the
  Brewfile installed appeared until the next reload. It now posts after.
- -homebrewManagerFinishedUpdating: cleared currentFormula on every
  reload, so an operation-triggered refresh blanked the detail pane and
  lost the user's place. The selection is now restored by name via a new
  -indexOfFormulaNamed: on the data source, falling back to clearing it
  only when the formula really is gone from the list.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

content.content:
## Problem

The formula detail pane shows wrong data against current Homebrew. All nine `brew info` fixtures in `CakebrewTests/` date from circa 2015 (they cite the retired `github.com/Homebrew/homebrew` Library/Formula path, ffmpeg 2.7.2, `--with-faac` options — e.g. `CakebrewTests/brewInfo_ffmpeg.txt:1,5`), and `BPFormula` walks the output positionally.

Verified against real brew on this machine: `brew info wget` now emits `==> wget: stable 1.25.0 (bottled), HEAD`, then for an installed formula `Installed (on request)`, `From:`, `License:` and `==> Installed Versions` where the 2015 format put the Cellar path. Some formulae add an `Aliases:` line. The positional walk (`Cakebrew/Models/BPFormula.m:357-397`) therefore assigns `installPath` the literal string `Installed (on request)`, which is displayed verbatim at `Cakebrew/Controllers/BPSelectedFormulaViewController.m:143-145`. The `==> ` header strip runs only for casks (`Cakebrew/Models/BPFormula.m:323`, via `preprocessedCaskInformation` at `:236-266`).

No CI job ever runs the parsers against the real Homebrew preinstalled on the `macos-26` runner, so this class of breakage is invisible (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, whole file).

## Proposal

- Capture fresh fixtures from current brew as `brewInfo_modern_*.txt`: installed, not-installed, keg-only, with-conflicts, with-caveats, and one with an `Aliases:` line.
- TDD `-getInformation` to strip `==> ` for formulae too, and to skip the `Installed (on request)` / `From:` / `License:` / `==> Installed Versions` block when locating the install path. Assert `installPath`, `latestVersion`, `website` and `shortDescription`.
- Keep the legacy fixtures as back-compat cases.
- Add a **scheduled** (not PR-path) brew-compat job to `ci.yml` that feeds the runner's real `brew info wget`, `brew list --versions`, `brew outdated --verbose`, `brew outdated --cask --verbose`, `brew list --cask --versions`, `brew services list --json` and `brew casks` through the matching parsers and fails on empty or malformed results.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Modern fixtures exist and are asserted field-by-field; legacy fixtures still pass
- [ ] `installPath` for an installed formula is a Cellar path, never `Installed (on request)`
- [ ] A fixture with an `Aliases:` line parses correctly
- [ ] A scheduled CI job exercises the parsers against real brew and fails on drift

## Notes

TDD: fixtures plus red assertions first. The scheduled job must not run on the PR path so upstream drift surfaces as its own alert rather than a red PR. CI runs on `macos-26`, which ships Homebrew.

name: Brew Compatibility

# Homebrew changes its output without warning — that is how `brew info` drifted
# until the detail pane started showing "Installed (on request)" as a location.
# Fixture tests cannot notice that, so this job pushes the *real* brew output
# on the runner through the same parsers.
#
# Deliberately NOT on the pull_request path: upstream drift is not the fault of
# whatever PR happens to be open, and it should surface as its own alert rather
# than a mysteriously red PR.
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 6 * * 1'   # Mondays, 06:17 UTC
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: brew-compat
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  brew-compat:
    name: Parsers vs. real brew
    runs-on: macos-26
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Show versions
        run: |
          brew --version
          xcodebuild -version

      - name: Ensure the fixtures the tests expect
        run: |
          # An installed formula (for the info/installed-list assertions) and a
          # known not-installed one. `|| true` so a preinstalled wget is fine.
          brew install wget || true
          brew uninstall --ignore-dependencies cowsay || true

      - name: Run parsers against real brew
        env:
          CAKEBREW_BREW_COMPAT: '1'
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          xcodebuild test \
            -workspace Cakebrew.xcworkspace \
            -scheme CakebrewTests \
            -destination 'platform=macOS' \
            -only-testing:CakebrewTests/BPBrewCompatibilityTests \
            CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO | xcpretty || exit 1

      - name: Capture fresh brew output on failure
        if: failure()
        run: |
          # The captured output is what a fixture refresh would be based on.
          mkdir -p brew-output
          for cmd in "info wget" "info cowsay" "list --versions" \
                     "outdated --verbose" "list --cask --versions" \
                     "services list --json"; do
            name=$(echo "$cmd" | tr ' /-' '___')
            brew $cmd > "brew-output/${name}.txt" 2>&1 || true
          done
          brew casks | head -50 > brew-output/casks_head.txt 2>&1 || true

      - name: Upload brew output
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: brew-output
          path: brew-output/

name: Brew Compatibility

# Homebrew changes its output without warning — that is how `brew info` drifted
# until the detail pane started showing "Installed (on request)" as a location.
# Fixture tests cannot notice that, so this job pushes the *real* brew output
# on the runner through the same parsers.
#
# Deliberately NOT on the pull_request path: upstream drift is not the fault of
# whatever PR happens to be open, and it should surface as its own alert rather
# than a mysteriously red PR.
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 6 * * 1'   # Mondays, 06:17 UTC
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: brew-compat
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  brew-compat:
    name: Parsers vs. real brew
    runs-on: macos-26
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Show versions
        run: |
          brew --version
          xcodebuild -version

      - name: Ensure the fixtures the tests expect
        run: |
          # An installed formula (for the info/installed-list assertions) and a
          # known not-installed one. `|| true` so a preinstalled wget is fine.
          brew install wget || true
          brew uninstall --ignore-dependencies cowsay || true

      - name: Run parsers against real brew
        env:
          CAKEBREW_BREW_COMPAT: '1'
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          xcodebuild test \
            -workspace Cakebrew.xcworkspace \
            -scheme CakebrewTests \
            -destination 'platform=macOS' \
            -only-testing:CakebrewTests/BPBrewCompatibilityTests \
            CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO | xcpretty || exit 1

      - name: Capture fresh brew output on failure
        if: failure()
        run: |
          # The captured output is what a fixture refresh would be based on.
          mkdir -p brew-output
          for cmd in "info wget" "info cowsay" "list --versions" \
                     "outdated --verbose" "list --cask --versions" \
                     "services list --json"; do
            name=$(echo "$cmd" | tr ' /-' '___')
            brew $cmd > "brew-output/${name}.txt" 2>&1 || true
          done
          brew casks | head -50 > brew-output/casks_head.txt 2>&1 || true

      - name: Upload brew output
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: brew-output
          path: brew-output/

Parse modern brew info and add a scheduled brew-compat job

All nine `brew info` fixtures dated from circa 2015 — they still cite the
retired github.com/Homebrew/homebrew Library/Formula path — and BPFormula
walked the output positionally. Current Homebrew:

- prefixes the header with "==> " (stripped for casks only, never formulae)
- may insert an "Aliases:" line after the homepage
- replaced the Cellar path with "Installed (on request)" / "(as dependency)"
- reports the actual build under "==> Installed Versions"
- adds a "License:" line

So for any installed formula the positional walk assigned installPath the
literal string "Installed (on request)", and the detail pane displayed it
verbatim. With an Aliases line it showed "Aliases: openssl, openssl@3.6".

The install-location scan now recognises both layouts: it skips the
Aliases/From/License metadata, returns nil for "Not installed", follows
the "Installed" marker to the Installed Versions block, and still accepts
the legacy Cellar path and keg-only shapes. All 35 legacy assertions keep
passing. The "==> " header prefix is now stripped for formulae too.

Modern brew reports no path here at all, so the pane's "Location:" label
becomes "Installed:" (Base xib plus all five translated .strings) and
shows what brew actually says: "wget 1.25.0 (92 files, 4.7MB) [Linked]".

Four fixtures captured from real brew — installed, not installed, an
Aliases line, and keg-only with caveats — asserted field by field.

Fixtures can't notice upstream drift, which is how this went unseen for
years, so BPBrewCompatibilityTests pushes the *real* brew output on the
machine through the same parsers: info, list --versions, outdated
--verbose, list --cask --versions, casks, and services list --json. It
skips unless CAKEBREW_BREW_COMPAT=1, so the hermetic suite is unaffected,
and a new scheduled workflow sets it weekly. Deliberately not on the PR
path: upstream drift isn't the open PR's fault.

The workflow passes it as TEST_RUNNER_CAKEBREW_BREW_COMPAT — xcodebuild
does not forward the shell environment to the test process, and with the
bare name every test skips and the job passes green. It also fails
explicitly if the run reports skips, so that can't regress silently.
Verified locally: all 7 pass against real brew.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

## Where things stand

| Issue | Branch | State |
|---|---|---|
| [#68](https://github.com/scottdensmore/Cakebrew/issues/68) streaming/deadlock | `fix/bptask-streaming` | **[PR #98](https://github.com/scottdensmore/Cakebrew/pull/98) — CI green** |
| [#69](https://github.com/scottdensmore/Cakebrew/issues/69) log views | `fix/streaming-log-views` | **[PR #99](https://github.com/scottdensmore/Cakebrew/pull/99) — CI green** |
| [#70](https://github.com/scottdensmore/Cakebrew/issues/70) catalog rebuild | `fix/skip-catalog-rebuild` | committed, unpushed |
| [#71](https://github.com/scottdensmore/Cakebrew/issues/71) info parser | `fix/modern-brew-info-parser` | committed, unpushed |

**193 tests, 0 failures, zero warnings** across the stack. Once auth is back I'll push the two branches, open their PRs, then merge all four in order (#99 and #70 need retargeting to `main` as each parent lands).

## On #70 and #71

**#70** — the fix is one tested policy function rather than 14 scattered booleans: only `update`, `tap`, `untap`, `bundle` can change catalog *membership*, so only they pay for the refetch. Unknown commands default to the cheap path, so a future operation can't silently reintroduce the 80-second stall. Two bugs came along in the same path: bundle import posted its reload *before* running the import (so it observed pre-import state), and every reload cleared `currentFormula`, blanking the detail pane — selection is now restored by name.

**#71** — you chose showing the installed-version line, so "Location:" is now "Installed:" in the xib and all five translations, displaying what brew actually reports. The parser handles both layouts; all 35 legacy assertions still pass. Four fixtures captured from real brew.

Two things worth your attention:

- **My compat workflow was broken and I nearly shipped it green.** `xcodebuild` doesn't forward the shell environment to the test process, so `CAKEBREW_BREW_COMPAT: '1'` meant every test skipped and the job passed. I only caught it because I ran the job locally instead of trusting it. It now uses `TEST_RUNNER_CAKEBREW_BREW_COMPAT` and **fails explicitly if the run reports skips** — a compat job that can silently pass is worse than none. Verified: 7/7 pass against your real brew.
- **#71's parser rewrite is the riskiest change in the batch.** It's well covered, but it touches the code path behind every formula you click. Worth a real human look before merge.

Your token now dies roughly every 15–20 minutes even after a clean `logout`/`login`. That's not normal expiry and it's cost us four interruptions. Before the next session it's worth checking whether something is clearing the login keychain — or sidestepping it entirely with a fine-grained PAT exported as `GH_TOKEN`, which bypasses the keyring the `gh` credential helper is reading from.

Closes #70.

> **Stacked on #99.** Base is `fix/streaming-log-views` so the diff shows only
> this change; I'll retarget to `main` as the parents land.

## What was broken

Fourteen mutating operations ended in `-sendDelegateFormulaeUpdatedCall`, which
landed in `-homebrewInterfaceDidUpdateFormulae` and unconditionally called
`reloadFromInterfaceRebuildingCache:YES`. The `YES` short-circuits the cache
guard, forcing both `brew formulae` and `brew casks` — the catalogs AGENTS.md
documents as **80+ seconds cold**.

So pinning a formula, unpinning it, or running Doctor — none of which can
change which packages exist — refetched both full catalogs plus all eight list
calls, with no progress shown and the user's selection discarded.

## What changed

The decision now lives in one tested place. Only commands that change catalog
*membership* — `update`, `tap`, `untap`, `bundle` — ask for the refetch;
install, uninstall, upgrade, pin, unpin, doctor and export do not. Unknown
commands default to the cheap path, so a new operation can't silently
reintroduce the stall. The delegate call carries that flag to the manager.

Two related fixes in the same path:

- `runBrewImportToolWithPath:` posted its reload **before** running the import,
  so the refresh observed pre-import state and nothing the Brewfile installed
  appeared until the next reload. It now posts after.
- `-homebrewManagerFinishedUpdating:` cleared `currentFormula` on every reload,
  so an operation-triggered refresh blanked the detail pane and lost the user's
  place. The selection is restored by name via a new `-indexOfFormulaNamed:`,
  falling back to clearing only when the formula really is gone from the list.

## Testing

`BPCatalogRefreshPolicyTests` pins the classification per command, including
the conservative default. `BPFormulaeDataSourceTests` covers the new row
lookup, including the absent case (so an uninstalled formula can't be confused
with row 0).

- Build: **zero warnings**
- Unit suite: **180 tests, 0 failures**

Per the issue's note, service operations and `runCleanupWithReturnBlock:` still
post nothing — left as they are.

Closes #71.

> **Stacked on #100.** Base is `fix/skip-catalog-rebuild` so the diff shows
> only this change; I'll retarget to `main` as the parents land.

## What was broken

All nine `brew info` fixtures dated from circa 2015 — they still cite the
retired `github.com/Homebrew/homebrew` Library/Formula path — and `BPFormula`
walked the output positionally. Current Homebrew:

- prefixes the header with `==> ` (stripped for casks only, never formulae)
- may insert an `Aliases:` line after the homepage
- replaced the Cellar path with `Installed (on request)` / `(as dependency)`
- reports the actual build under `==> Installed Versions`
- adds a `License:` line

So for **any installed formula** the positional walk assigned `installPath` the
literal string `Installed (on request)`, displayed verbatim in the detail pane.
With an Aliases line it showed `Aliases: openssl, openssl@3.6`.

## What changed

The install-location scan recognises both layouts: it skips the
Aliases/From/License metadata, returns nil for `Not installed`, follows the
`Installed` marker to the Installed Versions block, and still accepts the
legacy Cellar path and keg-only shapes. **All 35 legacy assertions keep
passing.** The `==> ` prefix is now stripped for formulae too.

Modern brew reports no path here at all, so the pane's **"Location:" label
becomes "Installed:"** (Base xib plus all five translated `.strings`) and shows
what brew actually says: `wget 1.25.0 (92 files, 4.7MB) [Linked]`.

## The scheduled compat job

Fixtures can't notice upstream drift — which is exactly how this went unseen
for years. `BPBrewCompatibilityTests` pushes the **real** brew output on the
machine through the same parsers: `info`, `list --versions`,
`outdated --verbose`, `list --cask --versions`, `casks`, and
`services list --json`. It skips unless the env var is set, so the hermetic
suite is unaffected, and a new weekly workflow sets it. Deliberately **not** on
the PR path: upstream drift isn't the open PR's fault.

One trap worth flagging for review: `xcodebuild` does not forward the shell
environment to the test process, so the obvious `CAKEBREW_BREW_COMPAT: '1'`
makes every test skip and the job pass **green**. It uses
`TEST_RUNNER_CAKEBREW_BREW_COMPAT` and additionally **fails if the run reports
skips**, so that can't regress silently.

## Testing

Four fixtures captured from real brew — installed, not installed, an Aliases
line, and keg-only with caveats — asserted field by field.

- Build: **zero warnings**
- Unit suite: **193 tests, 0 failures** (7 compat tests skipped, as intended)
- Compat job run locally against real brew: **7/7 pass**
- Detail pane checked visually under `-BPMockBrew`: label reads "Installed:",
  layout intact

This is the riskiest change of the four — it touches the code path behind every
formula you click — so it's worth a real look rather than a rubber stamp.
